pairs.subject: admission-queue
pairs.evidence: app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:221 The live event buffer grows without an enforced depth bound or shed policy, so failed synchronization can accumulate an unlimited backlog despite the decoder's restoration limits.

techniques.evidence: app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:294 Flush erases reasoned refusals, including the receiving route's PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE response, into a generic exception and subsequently false; callers cannot distinguish refusal from transport failure.
app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkDraft.ts:64 Candidate-writable JSON is fully materialized before any size or count check; subsequent filtering and truncation cannot protect the parsing allocation.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx:64 This path persists browser storage rather than calculating admission capacity from platform-free and allocator-reserved resources; no pooling denominator is involved.
app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:221 Recording appends without checking depth; MAX_PENDING_EVENTS applies only when decoding a restored draft, rather than when admitting live events.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx:207 This browser component schedules telemetry delivery; it does not promote expensive jobs onto a host execution pool whose pressure would select admission.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkDraft.ts:50 Drafts and their local buffers are scoped to one candidate token; this context does not arbitrate a shared queue containing competing origins or urgency classes.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:269 The buffer delivers to its session endpoint rather than dispatching waiters among worker pools; worker fungibility and queue partitioning are not decisions made here.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:311 Delivery uses retryable HTTP requests while retaining local state; no correlated refusal tears down an expensive population of long-lived transport callers.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx:22 The relevant storage threshold rejects a write rather than killing or restarting this component; no destructive watchdog threshold governs its backlog.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:227 Live edits accept arbitrary-length contents without charging an aggregate resource budget; limits applied during draft restoration do not bound live persistence or outgoing payloads.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:257 An eight-second flush interval exists, but each flush takes the entire backlog without a per-drain cap; the receiving route retains only the first 500 events.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:323 The inspected work records candidate actions and delivers their requested submission or chat; it contains no speculative prefetch or redundant fan-out class.
app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:272 The outgoing batch carries occurrence timestamps but no promotion timestamp or separate buffer-wait measurement, leaving synchronization wait unreported.

app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkSync.ts:223 Event recording proceeds asynchronously with intentionally buffered delivery; there is no synchronous caller deadline near one service time that would select zero depth.
